summary: This program builds a list of farmers' market products and then uses stream pipelines to pull out the set of vendor names, build a price menu for one vendor, and compute discounted prices for that vendor's items. It shows how `map` transforms each element of a stream into something new.

lines.text: `Collectors` supplies the recipes used at the end of a pipeline to gather results into a `List` or a `Set`.
Extra products are added so that one vendor, Baker's Lane, owns several items and the vendor-specific pipelines have something interesting to work on.
A `Set` is the right choice here because each vendor appears on several products and a set silently drops the duplicates.
Storing the vendor name in a variable means the same value can be reused for both the menu and the discount pipeline.
`forEach` walks the finished list, and the method reference `System.out::println` is shorthand for a lambda that prints each string.
The discount is passed as a fraction, so 0.10 means ten percent off; keeping it as a parameter makes the method reusable for any sale.
`stream()` turns the list into a flow of elements that the following operations process one at a time.
This is the heart of `map`: a stream of `MarketProduct` objects becomes a stream of vendor name strings.
Filtering after the map discards missing or empty vendor names so they never reach the result.
Collecting into a set produces each distinct vendor exactly once, with no ordering guarantee.
Only products belonging to the requested vendor survive, and `equalsIgnoreCase` makes the match forgiving about capitalization.
Here `map` turns each product into a display line, with `%.2f` formatting the price to two decimal places like real money.
The transformed strings are gathered into a `List` that the caller can print or reuse.
Converting the discount into a multiplier once, outside the pipeline, avoids recomputing it for every product.
Each price is mapped to its discounted value, and `Math.max` guards against a negative result if the discount fraction were ever greater than one.
